answer: A yarrow certifies an operator's identities only as quartz tokens wired onto one timber frame. Each new token must be spliced into the live bus, so the yarrow extends the frame by one more unit of timber than the last before sealing; a second frame is certified only by cutting it from the first frame's bus and carrying the length measured in quartz. A thousand identities cost 500,500 units of timber, and spare tokens rented elsewhere cannot shorten the bus.
